title: What If I Don't Have Enough Experience?

cues.en: What do I do if I don't have enough experience?
cues.zh: 經驗不足時，我該怎麼辦？

cues.en: What if I'm underqualified for a job?
cues.zh: 如果我的資歷不符合工作要求呢？

cues.en: In this video, we're going to talk about what to do if you don't have enough experience.
cues.zh: 這支影片要談談，經驗不足時該怎麼做。

cues.en: This is the experience cheat code, because this doesn't mean that it's game over for you.
cues.zh: 這是累積經驗的密技，因為經驗不足不代表你就出局了。

cues.en: There are ways to show experience, even if you might not have too much experience in the industry.
cues.zh: 即使產業經驗不多，還是有方法能展現經驗。

cues.en: First off, what if you are underqualified for a job?
cues.zh: 首先，如果你的資歷不符合職務要求呢？

cues.en: You're looking at a job application and you're saying to yourself, no way, I am not qualified for this job.
cues.zh: 看著職缺，你心想：不可能，我根本不符合資格。

cues.en: Well, first of all, you should have this mentality in mind when applying to jobs.
cues.zh: 首先，求職時應該抱持這樣的心態。

cues.en: Remember the law.
cues.zh: 記得那條原則。

cues.en: Don't be a junior.
cues.zh: 別把自己當成初階人員。

cues.en: You should be applying to jobs that you feel are under qualified for.
cues.zh: 你應該應徵那些讓你覺得自己還不夠格的工作。

cues.en: That means you should be applying to jobs that are hard, that you think are tough.
cues.zh: 也就是應徵有難度、讓你覺得很有挑戰的工作。

cues.en: If a job is asking you to do something that you already know that you already feel confident in, then
cues.zh: 如果一份工作要求的事，你已經會做、也很有信心，

cues.en: you should be asking yourself, what am I going to learn on this job if I'm already good at everything that they list?
cues.zh: 那你應該問自己：職缺列出的事我都很拿手了，那我能在這份工作學到什麼？

cues.en: Am I actually going to learn on this job?
cues.zh: 我真的能從中學到東西嗎？

cues.en: Is this job going to put things on my resume that will make me get better?
cues.zh: 這份工作能替履歷增加經歷，讓我進步，

cues.en: To be in a better position to get promoted in the future?
cues.zh: 未來更有機會升遷嗎？

cues.en: Or am I just doing this simple job?
cues.zh: 還是我只是在做一份簡單的工作，

cues.en: The same thing that I already know what to do?
cues.zh: 重複做自己早就會的事？

cues.en: So you have to and you should be applying to jobs that you think are really, really tough because those are the jobs that help you grow.
cues.zh: 所以你必須、也應該應徵那些覺得非常困難的工作，因為那些工作才能幫助你成長。

cues.en: And finally, you have to keep in mind that job postings are put in order to weed out the weak candidates.
cues.zh: 最後，你得記得，刊登職缺要求，是為了篩掉較弱的求職者。

cues.en: People put way more years of experience than the job actually requires just to make sure that they don't get any junior weak candidates.
cues.zh: 有些人把要求的年資寫得比工作實際需要的高很多，就是要避免初階、較弱的求職者應徵。

cues.en: I have seen way too many of these job applications created by non-technical or just human resources people, just making the job sound tougher than it actually is.
cues.zh: 我看過太多這類職缺，由非技術人員或人資撰寫，把工作描述得比實際更難。

cues.en: To remove these weak minded people from applying because they get thousands of applications.
cues.zh: 因為應徵者有上千人，他們想讓這些心態不夠堅定的人不敢投履歷。

cues.en: So next time you see an application and you think, oh boy, I'm never going to get this job.
cues.zh: 所以下次看到職缺，心想「天啊，我永遠不可能拿到這份工作」時，

cues.en: Well, that's a tough job and that's what you want.
cues.zh: 想想，那是有難度的工作，也正是你想要的。

cues.en: That's what you should be applying to.
cues.zh: 那才是你應該去應徵的工作。

cues.en: Because if you look at a job application and you feel confident you are qualified for this job, then
cues.zh: 因為如果看到職缺，你覺得很有信心，認為自己完全符合資格，

cues.en: maybe you should be asking yourself if you should be applying to more difficult jobs, because, I mean, if you don't try, the answer is always no.
cues.zh: 或許就該問問自己，是不是應該挑戰更難的工作。畢竟，不嘗試，答案永遠是否定的。

cues.en: Every application should be a long shot.
cues.zh: 每一次應徵，都應該是成功機會不高的挑戰。

cues.en: Otherwise, you're doing it wrong.
cues.zh: 否則，你的方法就不對。

cues.en: Remember, you're not swimming with others.
cues.zh: 記得，你不是要跟著別人游。

cues.en: You're your own fish, carving your own way.
cues.zh: 你是獨立的一條魚，要開創自己的路。

cues.en: You want room to grow.
cues.zh: 你需要成長空間。

cues.en: You want to dream big.
cues.zh: 你要敢於做大夢。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: But let's be honest.
cues.zh: 但老實說，

cues.en: There's a bit of a problem here, right?
cues.zh: 這裡還有個問題，對吧？

cues.en: You want to dream big, but you might have a bit of a roadblock.
cues.zh: 你想做大夢，但可能遇到一些阻礙。

cues.en: What if you simply don't have enough experience?
cues.zh: 如果你就是沒有足夠的經驗呢？

cues.en: What if you're actually just starting in this industry or in your field?
cues.zh: 如果你真的才剛踏入這個產業或領域呢？

cues.en: You see, I don't love resumes, and I don't think a lot of people do either.
cues.zh: 我不喜歡履歷，我想很多人也不喜歡。

cues.en: But sometimes without a resume, you cannot really get an interview.
cues.zh: 但有時沒有履歷，就真的拿不到面試機會。

cues.en: And in order to have a good resume, you need to have something to put on the resume, like great experience.
cues.zh: 要有一份好履歷，就得有東西可寫，例如很棒的經歷。

cues.en: Here's the catch, though.
cues.zh: 但矛盾就在這裡。

cues.en: How can you have great experience if you're just getting started?
cues.zh: 才剛開始，怎麼可能有很棒的經歷？

cues.en: It's like you have no hope if you're a beginner, right?
cues.zh: 好像新手就完全沒希望了，對吧？

cues.en: Or if you don't have work experience because you can't get a job.
cues.zh: 或者，因為找不到工作，所以沒有工作經驗。

cues.en: What are you supposed to do?
cues.zh: 那到底該怎麼辦？

cues.en: Maybe you're just out of school, just graduated, or you're changing careers and you literally have zero experience.
cues.zh: 你可能剛離開學校、剛畢業，或正在轉職，真的完全沒有經驗。

cues.en: Well not quite.
cues.zh: 其實未必。

cues.en: As with everything in this course, there's a regular way of doing things that everybody else follows.
cues.zh: 和這門課其他內容一樣，做事情有大家都遵循的一般方法，

cues.en: Then there's the smart way, the unique way that we're going to do.
cues.zh: 也有我們要採用的聰明、獨特的方法。

cues.en: Remember, we're not swimming with others.
cues.zh: 記得，我們不隨著別人游。

cues.en: We're our own fish.
cues.zh: 我們是獨立的一條魚。

cues.en: You see, experience doesn't just come from working at another company.
cues.zh: 經驗並不只來自曾在其他公司任職。

cues.en: There are many ways that you can demonstrate experience without a past job experience.
cues.zh: 即使沒有過去的工作經歷，也有很多方式能展現經驗。

cues.en: And here you'll find my favorite ways to showcase and to prove you can get the job done to employers.
cues.zh: 接下來，我要分享最喜歡的幾種方式，向雇主展示、證明你有能力完成工作。

cues.en: Now, you won't have to do every single one of these, but two out of five.
cues.zh: 不需要每一項都做，但五項裡做到兩項，

cues.en: Or even better, three out of five of these will be great at showcasing on your resume and making you stand out.
cues.zh: 更好的是做到三項，就很適合放進履歷，讓你脫穎而出。

cues.en: So let's go in order through these and see how we can add experience using these tools.
cues.zh: 我們依序看看，怎麼運用這些工具增加經驗。

cues.en: First, let's talk about LinkedIn.
cues.zh: 首先談 LinkedIn。

cues.en: Now we have a whole section on LinkedIn.
cues.zh: 我們有一整節介紹 LinkedIn。

cues.en: So this is just a brief overview.
cues.zh: 所以這裡只做簡短概述。

cues.en: But on LinkedIn you can demonstrate experience by just simply showing all the things you've done.
cues.zh: 在 LinkedIn 上，只要展示你做過的事情，就能展現經驗。

cues.en: I'm going to leave my profile for you so you can actually take a look.
cues.zh: 我會提供自己的個人檔案，讓你實際看看。

cues.en: But if you look at my experience through my years, I have the most random experience.
cues.zh: 但如果看我歷年經驗，會發現我的經歷非常五花八門。

cues.en: I was a tennis club manager.
cues.zh: 我當過網球俱樂部經理。

cues.en: I was teaching English in Japan, I was a salesperson, I was a tour director.
cues.zh: 在日本教過英文，當過業務、旅遊領隊。

cues.en: I started a adventure racing company.
cues.zh: 我創辦過冒險競賽公司。

cues.en: I did sailing trips.
cues.zh: 辦過帆船旅行。

cues.en: I even have my yoga instructor certificate.
cues.zh: 我甚至有瑜伽教練證照。

cues.en: You see, these are all kind of random, but they show me doing things, doing things and swimming on
cues.zh: 這些看似不太相關，但都證明我有實際行動，沿著

cues.en: my own path, showing my unique skills that I'm stacking.
cues.zh: 自己的道路前進，展現逐步累積的獨特技能。

cues.en: And on LinkedIn.
cues.zh: 而在 LinkedIn，

cues.en: There's interesting things you can do, like endorsing skills.
cues.zh: 還有一些有趣的功能，例如技能背書。

cues.en: As a matter of fact, you can have other people endorse your skills that you want and recommend you
cues.zh: 你可以請別人替想強調的技能背書，並在 LinkedIn 個人檔案上

cues.en: on your LinkedIn profile, and you can use these to bolster your LinkedIn profile.
cues.zh: 寫推薦，藉此強化自己的個人檔案。

cues.en: Again, we'll talk about this in the LinkedIn section.
cues.zh: 我們會在 LinkedIn 那一節再談。

cues.en: But we actually have a ZM Academy group where you can actually share endorsements with each other and
cues.zh: 我們其實有個 ZTM Academy 群組，可以互相分享技能背書，

cues.en: promote your blogs.
cues.zh: 推廣自己的部落格、

cues.en: Your articles get recommendations from other ZM students as a way to bolster your LinkedIn, and also showcase some other things that we're going to talk about later.
cues.zh: 文章，並取得其他 ZTM 學員的推薦，強化 LinkedIn 個人檔案，也展示稍後會談的其他成果。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: But that's just LinkedIn.
cues.zh: 但這只是 LinkedIn。

cues.en: You've bolstered a bit of your LinkedIn profile.
cues.zh: 你稍微強化了自己的 LinkedIn 個人檔案，

cues.en: You have some endorsements, some recommendations.
cues.zh: 有了技能背書、推薦，

cues.en: Maybe you write a couple of posts, which we'll talk about on LinkedIn.
cues.zh: 或許寫了幾篇貼文；我們也會在 LinkedIn 部分談這件事。

cues.en: What about GitHub?
cues.zh: 那 GitHub 呢？

cues.en: Well, GitHub.
cues.zh: 說到 GitHub，

cues.en: I've already shown you how to use it to create a simple portfolio website, but it's actually a great tool for gaining experience.
cues.zh: 我已經示範過，如何用它建立簡單的作品集網站，但它其實也是累積經驗的好工具。

cues.en: You see, GitHub is a great way to demonstrate that not only do you code, but you work on projects with others.
cues.zh: GitHub 很適合展現你不只會寫程式，也能和別人一起做專案。

cues.en: So it's not just for programmers.
cues.zh: 所以它不只是給程式設計師用的。

cues.en: It can be a designer, you can be a writer, you can use GitHub because GitHub allows all sorts of files to be uploaded and shared.
cues.zh: 設計師、寫作者也能使用，因為 GitHub 能上傳、分享各種檔案。

cues.en: You can load PDFs, images, designs and others.
cues.zh: 你可以放 PDF、圖片、設計稿等。

cues.en: But for experienced, the number one thing you can do with GitHub is to start making what's called commits and making sure that you have a good history of things that you've done.
cues.zh: 但若要展現經驗，使用 GitHub 最重要的事，就是開始建立 commit 提交，確保留下良好的成果歷程。

cues.en: You see, this is your git history.
cues.zh: 這就是你的 Git 歷史紀錄。

cues.en: This shows possible recruiters your activity on GitHub.
cues.zh: 它能向可能接觸你的招募人員展示 GitHub 活動。

cues.en: And the longer this history is, the more experienced, or at least the more experienced it looks like you have.
cues.zh: 這份歷史越長，經驗就越多，至少看起來越有經驗。

cues.en: This essentially tracks your activity on GitHub.
cues.zh: 它基本上就是追蹤你在 GitHub 上的活動。

cues.en: So if you're doing something every single day on GitHub, putting up code, putting up projects, this will be filled with green.
cues.zh: 如果你每天都在 GitHub 做事，上傳程式、專案，這裡就會充滿綠色。

cues.en: And by the way, there are some unique tricks to make it look like you're way more active than you are.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，有些特別技巧能讓你看起來比實際活躍得多。

cues.en: For example, you can use some of these tools, which I'm going to share with you after this video to
cues.zh: 例如，這支影片後我會分享一些工具，讓你

cues.en: make cool little GitHub commits that look like this, that actually makes you stand out, and some recruiters are going to stumble over it and say, wow, that's kind of funny.
cues.zh: 做出像這樣有趣的 GitHub commit 圖案，讓你與眾不同。有些招募人員看到會說，哇，真有趣。

cues.en: Kind of cool how they have that.
cues.zh: 這種呈現方式滿酷的。

cues.en: Again, you're standing out from the crowd.
cues.zh: 再次讓你從人群中脫穎而出。

cues.en: Another way to use GitHub for experience is contributing and participating in what's called open source projects.
cues.zh: 另一種透過 GitHub 累積經驗的方式，是參與所謂的開放原始碼專案，做出貢獻。

cues.en: For example, I've created a zero to mastery organization where we have a ton of open source projects
cues.zh: 例如，我建立了 Zero to Mastery 組織，裡面有很多開放原始碼專案，

cues.en: that are built by the student community and that you can contribute to, and they're made specifically for you to mess up, make mistakes, get experience.
cues.zh: 由學員社群共同打造，你也能參與。這些專案特別就是讓你嘗試、犯錯、累積經驗用的。

cues.en: Nobody's going to yell at you if you make a mistake on one of these projects.
cues.zh: 在這些專案裡犯錯，不會有人對你大吼。

cues.en: These are just fun projects that are open source that you can contribute to and eventually actually add to your resume.
cues.zh: 這些都是有趣的開放原始碼專案，你可以貢獻，最後真的把它們放進履歷。

cues.en: And you can do as much or as little as you want with these open source projects, you can update a simple
cues.zh: 參與程度由你決定，可以多也可以少。你可以更新簡單的

cues.en: text Readme file, you can add designs, you can change code and contributing to open source projects.
cues.zh: README 文字檔、加入設計、修改程式。參與開放原始碼專案，

cues.en: Well, recruiters love seeing this because this demonstrates that you can work with others and also
cues.zh: 招募人員很喜歡看到，因為這能證明你可以與人合作，

cues.en: with things like GitHub and version control and in working on actual projects, and Ztm has community events throughout the year.
cues.zh: 也能使用 GitHub 和版本控制，參與真正的專案。ZTM 全年也有社群活動。

cues.en: For example, we have Octoberfest in October where we work on open source projects like Animation Nation.
cues.zh: 例如十月的開源活動，我們會一起做 Animation Nation 之類的開放原始碼專案。

cues.en: Where students just share some of their animations with the community.
cues.zh: 學員在裡面和社群分享自己的動畫。

cues.en: My favorite one that students have built, and this happened just this year, is Ztm Quest.
cues.zh: 我最喜歡的一個學員作品，是今年才做出來的 ZTM Quest。

cues.en: They've literally made a game that's right, a ztm game where you can just walk around like you're playing Game Boy.
cues.zh: 他們真的做出了一款遊戲，沒錯，是 ZTM 遊戲，可以像玩 Game Boy 一樣走來走去。

cues.en: How cool is that?
cues.zh: 很酷吧？

cues.en: And this was built by students, and you can work on this project if you want and add it to your portfolio, or at least add it to your experience.
cues.zh: 這是學員做的，你也可以參與，把它加進作品集，至少也能算成經歷。

cues.en: The next one is portfolio website.
cues.zh: 下一項是作品集網站。

cues.en: And as I've shown you in the previous video, when we did a simple portfolio website.
cues.zh: 正如之前的影片，我們做簡單作品集網站時示範的，

cues.en: You don't need to be a full stack developer or a designer to have your own website.
cues.zh: 不需要是全端開發人員或設計師，也能擁有自己的網站。

cues.en: The idea is that a portfolio website is something you build to showcase your big projects, which we talk about in the next point, 1 to 2 big projects.
cues.zh: 作品集網站的用意，就是展示大型專案；這是下一點要談的一到兩個大型專案。

cues.en: So portfolio website is an online presence that already makes you stand out because that's your experience.
cues.zh: 所以，作品集網站是一種網路上的個人展示，光是建立它，就已經讓你脫穎而出，因為那就是經驗。

cues.en: You put something online and inside it, you're going to have 1 to 2 big projects that are what I call Wow, projects that are going to impress employers and interviewers.
cues.zh: 你把成果放到網路上，網站裡再放一到兩個大型專案，也就是我所說會讓雇主、面試官驚嘆的專案。

cues.en: And the idea of these projects in your portfolio is that they're going to be set up in a way that it's something that you're going to be able to speak about in your interview, about how you built the website,
cues.zh: 作品集裡的專案，應該讓你能在面試時，談談網站如何建立、

cues.en: how you built the projects, and it gives you a good way to talk about your past experiences building these projects.
cues.zh: 專案如何打造，讓你有很好的方式，分享建立這些專案的經歷。

cues.en: But here's the problem.
cues.zh: 但問題來了。

cues.en: How do you build these big projects?
cues.zh: 這些大型專案要怎麼做？

cues.en: Well, first off, the good news is that you only need 1 to 2 big projects.
cues.zh: 首先，好消息是，你只需要一到兩個大型專案。

cues.en: Now, you can't really fake experience if you've never built anything beyond a simple to do list.
cues.zh: 如果從沒做過比簡單待辦清單更進階的東西，就很難展現真正的經驗。

cues.en: A hello world.
cues.zh: 或者只有 Hello World，

cues.en: Just something basic that you can find on YouTube.
cues.zh: 只有 YouTube 上找得到的基礎範例，

cues.en: You're not going to get good jobs.
cues.zh: 是拿不到好工作的。

cues.en: When I talk about 1 to 2 big projects, I mean big, impressive projects.
cues.zh: 我說的一到兩個大型專案，是真的大型、令人印象深刻的專案。

cues.en: The problem is that when people think about learning, they think about building 100 projects as they learn.
cues.zh: 問題是，很多人想到學習，就覺得要邊學邊做一百個專案。

cues.en: So they do a project today, build a small project that's not really impressive.
cues.zh: 於是今天做一個小專案，卻沒什麼亮點。

cues.en: A simple calculator, a simple tic tac toe app.
cues.zh: 簡單的計算機、簡單的井字遊戲應用程式。

cues.en: They build very, very simple projects.
cues.zh: 做的都是非常簡單的專案。

cues.en: And when a recruiter sees this, you look like any other candidate.
cues.zh: 招募人員看到，會覺得你跟其他求職者沒兩樣。

cues.en: It's not really impressive.
cues.zh: 並不特別令人印象深刻。

cues.en: It's something that anybody can build in a day or two.
cues.zh: 那些東西，任何人花一兩天都能做出來。

cues.en: And frankly, no recruiter is going to read your entire portfolio, go through all your 30 projects.
cues.zh: 而且老實說，沒有招募人員會讀完整份作品集，逐一看完三十個專案。

cues.en: They don't have time for that, and they don't care about you.
cues.zh: 他們沒時間，也不會那麼在乎你。

cues.en: Most of the time they want to hear about your most difficult, the hardest, the biggest project you worked on.
cues.zh: 多數時候，他們想聽的是你做過最困難、最艱鉅、最大型的專案。

cues.en: And here is where Ztm comes in.
cues.zh: 這就是 ZTM 能提供協助的地方。

cues.en: We're actually focused on helping you build these big projects in every course that you do.
cues.zh: 我們每門課都很重視，協助你打造這類大型專案。

cues.en: For example, this is one of my favorites in the three.js course, which is right over here.
cues.zh: 例如，這裡的 Three.js 課程中，就有一個我很喜歡的範例。

cues.en: We actually teach you to build this.
cues.zh: 我們會教你做出這個。

cues.en: Which can actually turn into your portfolio if you want to.
cues.zh: 你願意的話，它甚至可以成為你的作品集。

cues.en: You have a little player, this 3D player that you walk around and look at that you can say, hey, this is my portfolio.
cues.zh: 你能操控這個小小的 3D 角色走來走去。看看，你可以說：「嘿，這就是我的作品集。」

cues.en: And as you walk along you have all your projects listed here.
cues.zh: 邊走，就會看到列在這裡的所有專案。

cues.en: How cool is that?
cues.zh: 很酷吧？

cues.en: In the unity course, for example, we help you build a real life game that you can play and demonstrate
cues.zh: 例如 Unity 課程，我們協助你做出一款真正能玩的遊戲，讓你能展示

cues.en: to your employers.
cues.zh: 給雇主看。

cues.en: These are big projects that most people wouldn't build because it takes days to build them.
cues.zh: 這些都是多數人不會做的大型專案，因為需要花好幾天才能完成。

cues.en: In my own course, where I teach you to become a full stack developer, we build a face recognition app.
cues.zh: 在我教你成為全端開發人員的課程中，我們會打造人臉辨識應用程式。

cues.en: And this app, well, it has a front end using react back end using a RESTful API server.
cues.zh: 這個應用程式，前端使用 React，後端使用 RESTful API 伺服器。

cues.en: With express we deploy to production.
cues.zh: 搭配 Express，並部署到正式環境。

cues.en: We create session management, authenticated routes.
cues.zh: 我們建立工作階段管理，以及需要驗證身分的路由。

cues.en: We store user information and username and hashed passwords in a secure database using Postgres.
cues.zh: 使用 Postgres，在安全的資料庫裡儲存使用者資訊、使用者名稱，以及雜湊後的密碼。

cues.en: We deploy our app with Docker and we use Reddis for session management and caching.
cues.zh: 用 Docker 部署應用程式，並以 Redis 處理工作階段管理與快取。

cues.en: Now all of that may not mean a lot to you, but having something like a one big project that you can talk about, like I just did, sounds really impressive to employers.
cues.zh: 你可能還不太理解這些，但就像剛才那樣，能談論自己做過的大型專案，會讓雇主印象深刻。

cues.en: Each of our courses creates one of these 1 to 2 big projects, but we also have a special section under
cues.zh: 我們每門課都會做出一到兩個這樣的大型專案，此外也有特別的

cues.en: the project format where you can build a ton of really cool projects that are what we call Wow projects.
cues.zh: 專案類別，讓你打造許多很酷、我們稱為會讓人驚嘆的專案。

cues.en: These are the sort of projects that most people won't build.
cues.zh: 這些是多數人不會動手做的專案。

cues.en: It'll take you a long time to build them, but once you build them, you have 1 or 2 of these on your resume and it's going to really blow employers minds.
cues.zh: 需要花很長時間才能完成，但完成後，把一兩個放進履歷，真的能讓雇主大吃一驚。

cues.en: If I had no experience, I would immediately put one of these projects at the very top of my resume.
cues.zh: 如果我沒有經驗，會立刻把這類專案放在履歷最上方。

cues.en: Because here's the thing if you don't have work experience for your work experience, you just simply
cues.zh: 因為，如果沒有工作經歷，工作經驗欄就直接

cues.en: put this project, let's call the project the Smart brain app that you've built.
cues.zh: 寫這個專案，假設叫做你打造的 Smart Brain 應用程式。

cues.en: You'll put that as a title, and your job description was JavaScript developer or a full stack engineer.
cues.zh: 把它當成標題，職務則寫 JavaScript 開發人員或全端工程師。

cues.en: And inside the resume you talk about how you build that project because to a recruiter, it doesn't really matter if you worked at a certain company, at least when they first glance at your resume.
cues.zh: 在履歷裡說明你如何打造這個專案。對招募人員來說，至少第一眼看履歷時，你有沒有待過某家公司，不是那麼重要。

cues.en: Building an application on your own is what's impressive.
cues.zh: 能自己做出應用程式，才令人印象深刻。

cues.en: They couldn't care less about the company that you worked at, unless it's a big, well-known company.
cues.zh: 除非你待過知名大公司，否則他們根本不在意公司名稱。

cues.en: They just need to know that you build things that are real, that are big and complicated, and that you solved hard problems.
cues.zh: 他們只需要知道，你做過真實、大型而複雜的東西，而且解決過困難問題。

cues.en: So having 1 or 2 big projects that you can list on your experience is a great way to add to your resume.
cues.zh: 所以，在經歷裡列出一到兩個大型專案，是替履歷增加內容的好方法，

cues.en: If you don't have enough past work experience at companies.
cues.zh: 尤其是過去在公司的工作經驗不足時。

cues.en: And I actually have a few students who have used this technique to get interviews, even though they just learned how to code six months ago.
cues.zh: 我確實有幾位學員，用這個方法拿到面試，儘管他們六個月前才開始學寫程式。

cues.en: All right, final point, because this video is getting long and this is a blog.
cues.zh: 好，最後一點，因為影片已經有點長了，那就是部落格。

cues.en: This is another thing you can include in your resume, especially if it's related to a technology or a skill you're using and the company you're applying for is using now.
cues.zh: 這也可以放進履歷，尤其當內容與你使用的技術或技能有關，而目標公司目前也在使用它時。

cues.en: You can do this with YouTube videos as well, but I prefer writing because it's a lot faster, and frankly, it looks a lot more professional writing technical blog posts.
cues.zh: 你也可以製作 YouTube 影片，但我偏好寫作，因為快得多，而且老實說，撰寫技術文章看起來更專業。

cues.en: You can use AI tools to help you write.
cues.zh: 你可以使用 AI 工具協助寫作。

cues.en: You can brainstorm ideas, then use an AI tool like Claude or ChatGPT to help you write a technical
cues.zh: 先發想，再用 Claude 或 ChatGPT 之類的 AI 工具，協助撰寫技術

cues.en: blog post that you can put on your portfolio, and you can put this blog post on LinkedIn.
cues.zh: 部落格文章，放進作品集，也能分享到 LinkedIn。

cues.en: You can put this blog post on your website.
cues.zh: 你可以把文章放在自己的網站。

cues.en: You can even post it on GitHub.
cues.zh: 甚至發到 GitHub。

cues.en: But having this blog that you write can actually be an item on your resume that you maintain this technical blog where you write topics about your skill.
cues.zh: 經營這樣的部落格，本身就可以寫進履歷：你持續維護技術部落格，撰寫與自己技能相關的主題。

cues.en: They don't need to know how many readers your blog has, but the fact that you've started a blog on this specific skill that they need, that's impressive and that's experience.
cues.zh: 他們不需要知道部落格有多少讀者；你為了他們需要的特定技能建立部落格，本身就很亮眼，也是一種經驗。

cues.en: So let's review here.
cues.zh: 我們來回顧。

cues.en: What happens if you don't have enough experience?
cues.zh: 經驗不足時，怎麼辦？

cues.en: Well, all of these points will allow you to gain that experience, or at least show that you have experience without actually having traditional company work experience.
cues.zh: 這些方法都能幫你累積經驗，至少也能在沒有傳統公司任職經歷時，展現自己有經驗。

cues.en: All you need to do is start something on your own and build something like a project, or a portfolio, or a blog post.
cues.zh: 只需要自己開始做點事，打造專案、作品集，或寫一篇部落格文章。

cues.en: This shows initiative and let's be honest, the whole goal is to get an interview because all of this is to get an interview.
cues.zh: 這展現主動性。老實說，整體目標就是拿到面試，所有這些都是為了面試。

cues.en: The whole point of this section is to get that interview, because once we get in the door, once we get the interview, we're going to ace it because of the upcoming section on interviews.
cues.zh: 這一節的重點，就是取得面試機會。只要踏進門、拿到面試，接下來的面試章節就能幫我們表現出色。

cues.en: By taking this initiative, you're doing more than most people that hope to just land an interview by
cues.zh: 採取主動，已經比多數人做得更多；那些人只希望靠著

cues.en: sending a generic resume to hundreds and thousands of companies, just by simply clicking a couple of buttons.
cues.zh: 點幾個按鈕，把制式履歷寄給幾百、幾千家公司，就能得到面試。

cues.en: You'll immediately stand out from the crowd and give you something to put on your resume.
cues.zh: 你會立刻脫穎而出，也有東西能放進履歷。

cues.en: That, again is different than the average person.
cues.zh: 再次強調，這和一般人不同。

cues.en: Plus, you have the added benefit of having something to talk about on your actual interview.
cues.zh: 而且還有額外好處：真正面試時，你有內容可以談。

cues.en: Remember, nothing is given to you for free, and luck is for those who rather wait than go after what they want.
cues.zh: 記住，沒有什麼是免費送上門的；運氣，是留給寧可等待、也不追求自己目標的人。

cues.en: Don't depend on luck, because luck is exactly that a gamble.
cues.zh: 別依賴運氣，因為運氣就是一場賭博。

cues.en: So work hard for it by simply building something just for fun, such as a side project, you're showing how self-motivated and ambitious you are.
cues.zh: 所以努力爭取吧。即使只是為了好玩，做個業餘專案，也能展現你的自我驅動與企圖心。

cues.en: Experience doesn't mean on the job experience.
cues.zh: 經驗，不等於在職經驗。

cues.en: Experience means work.
cues.zh: 經驗，代表做過事。

cues.en: All of these things I've listed here answer this question.
cues.zh: 我列出的所有方法，都在回答這個問題。

cues.en: Do you have experience?
cues.zh: 你有經驗嗎？

cues.en: And if you do these, yes you do.
cues.zh: 如果做了這些，答案就是有。

cues.en: Finally, there are many things that you can add that are not specific to a technical skill that are still great for employers to see.
cues.zh: 最後，還有很多不屬於特定技術技能的事情，也很值得讓雇主看到。

cues.en: For example, did you work as a cashier in McDonald's?
cues.zh: 例如，你在麥當勞當過收銀員嗎？

cues.en: Well, you can now add the ability to manage people and communicate well with others to your resume.
cues.zh: 那你可以在履歷中加入管理人員、與他人良好溝通的能力。

cues.en: That's a great skill.
cues.zh: 那是很好的技能。

cues.en: Any skill that is related to getting the job done can be included.
cues.zh: 任何和完成工作有關的技能，都能列入。

cues.en: But be warned here, if let's say, for example, you only had six months of coding experience and you only learned to code six months ago because you want to apply to be a developer.
cues.zh: 但這裡要小心。假設你只有六個月的程式設計經驗，六個月前才因為想應徵開發人員而開始學程式，

cues.en: As an example, don't actually show that on the resume.
cues.zh: 以此為例，不要真的在履歷上強調這一點。

cues.en: It doesn't mean that you should lie, but to just hide that information because a recruiter only glances at your resume briefly.
cues.zh: 這不代表要說謊，而是先不呈現這項資訊，因為招募人員只會很快掃過履歷。

cues.en: They won't care if you're the best developer in the world, even though it's just been six months, it's too risky for them.
cues.zh: 就算你已經是全世界最好的開發人員，才學六個月這件事，對他們來說還是太冒險。

cues.en: Your resume is most likely going to get discarded, no matter how good of a developer you are.
cues.zh: 不管你多優秀，履歷很可能就被淘汰，

cues.en: If you just say, hey, I only have six months experience.
cues.zh: 只因為你說：「嘿，我只有六個月經驗。」

cues.en: If you don't have a lot of experience.
cues.zh: 如果經驗不多，

cues.en: Don't emphasize how little time you spent.
cues.zh: 就別強調自己花的時間有多短。

cues.en: Instead, try to stretch that and be vague about how many years of experience you have.
cues.zh: 相反地，盡量延伸經驗的呈現，對年資維持模糊。

cues.en: Remember, resumes are only good to get your foot in the door by tweaking your resume to show that you
cues.zh: 記得，履歷的作用只是讓你踏進門。調整履歷，展現

cues.en: have experience so that the recruiter thinks, oh, interviewing this person is low risk because they know what they are talking about is what you want to do.
cues.zh: 自己有經驗，讓招募人員覺得：「面試這個人風險不高，他知道自己在說什麼。」這才是你的目標。

cues.en: They want to know if you have past experience, if you've made good decisions in the past, have you worked on a challenging problem and solve them?
cues.zh: 他們想知道，你是否有過經驗、過去是否做過好決定，以及是否解決過有挑戰性的問題。

cues.en: If you're able to answer yes to that and show that on the resume, the recruiter is most likely going to ask you for an interview.
cues.zh: 如果答案是肯定的，也能在履歷中呈現，招募人員多半就會邀你面試。

cues.en: Over the next couple of videos, we're going to talk about how to make all of these stand out.
cues.zh: 接下來幾支影片，我們會談如何讓這些內容更突出，

cues.en: So it looks like you have the best experience possible.
cues.zh: 讓你的經驗看起來盡可能出色。

cues.en: So we still have a long way to go.
cues.zh: 所以，還有很長一段路要走。

cues.en: And we'll keep emphasizing this point.
cues.zh: 我們會持續強調這一點。

cues.en: I'll see you in the next one.
cues.zh: 下支影片見。

cues.en: Bye bye.
cues.zh: 再見。
